historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes state change but treats DediProg like an arbitrary remote utility and supplies no programmer, flash-chip, image-layout, verify or recovery contract.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires an operator-led vendor procedure, signed image, downtime, stable power, complete pre/post PCIe health and no blind retry.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity; adjacent row 1738 is a completed Final Audit baseline identity and was excluded from active Full Review sequencing.
historical_reviews.v3_1: DediProg commonly programs a specific nonvolatile device through a physical adapter or board fixture; the target is the flash chip and image region, not merely the enumerated PCIe function. Chip part number, voltage, pin/fixture orientation, erase/program/verify scope and preservation of board-specific data must be fixed before any write.

original_test_intent: Program the intended BRCM switch firmware with DediProg and prove that the switch and dependent PCIe fabric recover with the approved image.
original_method: Identify the exact switch board and flash device, use the vendor-approved DediProg hardware/software, fixture, voltage and image layout under an authorized local operator, back up and hash the original contents, program only the approved regions, run tool-level verify, restore the board safely, then compare authoritative running firmware and complete PCIe topology/health against owner-defined acceptance criteria.
manual_activity: An authorized hardware operator connects and operates the approved DediProg fixture; the platform/firmware owner approves the exact chip, image regions, criteria, downtime and recovery and decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Flash chip part number and voltage
Approved DediProg model, software and firmware
Image layout and protected board-specific regions
safety_requirements: Require explicit owner approval immediately before programming
Use authorized local hardware handling and ESD controls
Verify chip identity, voltage and orientation before contact
Back up and hash original contents
Do not guess image offset or program protected calibration/identity data
Stop on ID, erase, program or verify error
No blind retry, automatic power cycle or improvised rollback
agent_execution_scope: Observe and capture DediProg output supplied by the operator
Report without operating the programmer or deciding verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: An unresolved SSH command does not represent the source's DediProg hardware workflow and could target an unrelated host utility; filtered lspci ROM text cannot verify programmed contents or active firmware.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Follow the exact vendor DediProg hardware procedure for the identified flash chip: read/backup, erase/program approved image regions, verify against the image, then restore hardware and perform read-only running-version and complete PCIe health checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The DediProg flash objective and stated 5-minute activity are preserved, while recognizing that actual vendor programming, teardown and recovery time governs safe execution.

modernized_recommendation.status: FIXTURE-CONTROLLED SWITCH FLASH WITH CHIP-LEVEL VERIFY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed programming traveler that binds board serial, flash-chip ID, DediProg/fixture, voltage, image hash/layout, backup hash, operator, tool log and post-restore fabric health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the physical programming target and lifecycle rather than treating firmware flash as a generic remote executable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tool exit code can be successful while the wrong chip/region was written, and a byte verify can pass while the board fails to boot the intended active image; both chip-level and system-level checks are required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Criteria remain TBD, so execution readiness—not the review classification—remains gated until the owner publishes version, verify, boot, topology and recovery acceptance.

project_override_considerations: Define whether programming is in-circuit or socketed, required board power isolation, flash-chip voltage and pinout, full-image versus region writes, protected serial/calibration regions, expected DediProg ID/blank/program/verify results and system recovery criteria.
expected_evidence: Approved traveler with board/chip/fixture/image identities and hashes
DediProg device-ID, erase/program/verify output and exit status
Pre/post authoritative running firmware and complete PCIe topology/health
Published acceptance results, recovery status, no-retry/no-log-clear audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Procedure consistently request DediProg firmware programming. Criteria are explicitly incomplete rather than contradictory, and DeepSeek's remote command is an unsafe implementation mismatch.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The flash purpose and expected vendor artifacts are identifiable, so the review is REQUIRES rather than intrinsically BLOCKED. Actual execution must remain blocked until chip/image mapping, criteria and recovery are approved.

review_improvement: Reframes the test as chip- and fixture-specific programming with protected-region, backup, verify and system-recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: The enumerated PCIe switch is not sufficient identity for a DediProg write because the programmer addresses a physical flash device that may contain board-specific regions. Safe coverage must bind the chip electrical interface and image layout before writing, then separately prove both byte verification and the restored switch's active firmware/fabric behavior.
